title: Music in Cuba, Jamaica and Mexico
summary: Cuban bands, a jukebox dance in rural Jamaica, and Mexican mariachis.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Uh, do they have a lot of steel bands there? Not. Or are they mostly further?

No, not that I, further south. More, not that I know of. And I don't get the idea that I went all around, you know, trying to find it. I just heard what they have. They have some nice little bands, you know, trio or a quartet with guitars and stuff. And one of those, you know, those steel basses that vibrate, you know, they're just a box with a little vibrating. Yeah. They had those, but they were singing all, um, Spanish type songs, Cuban type of songs, not like the Calypso. I was in Jamaica a year ago, two years, nearly, ooh, two years ago. And it was fantastic when you could, uh, get way out in the hills, you know, where they didn't have any electricity or anything. Miles out, practically the jungle, you know, people living in huts and all that. And every Saturday night they'd have a dance and they'd bring a jukebox that was run from a battery on the truck. And they'd have all the Fats Domino records, all the Elvis records, all that, you know, I went out there expecting to hear the real Calypso because they had a bit if you dug it out. Yeah, same trouble. It's always interested me the way those, all the different, uh, forms that that kind of music has taken around the Caribbean and around this city and in Mexico too.
Some fine instrument, instrumental playing in Mexico. Mariachis, you know, trumpets. Yeah. Beautiful stuff.
